answer: Random-route intersection resists sybils: an identity is accepted only if its short random walks through the attestation graph meet the routes of already-trusted nodes — which honest fast-mixing nodes do reliably. A walnut-dense fake cluster sits behind a sparse cut, so walks entering it rarely escape to mirror an honest route; intersection probability collapses with the bottleneck's narrowness. A plume of internal fakes cannot forge intersections — acceptance tracks the few honest edges crossing the cut, not internal density. Precondition: honest subgraph mixes well, attack cut sparse.
